dedupe_keys.name: gnss positioning and ionospheric response in mexico during the 10 may 2024 geomagnetic superstorm geodetic and low cost receivers

description: This open-access paper analyses how the 10 May 2024 geomagnetic superstorm changed ionospheric total electron content and GNSS positioning at stations across Mexico. It finds well-defined positive and negative storm phases at all stations, with dayside TEC increases reaching plus or minus 180 percent at northern stations attributed to prompt penetration electric fields, followed by nighttime depletions of 58 to 77 percent with a persistent latitudinal gradient. Low-cost GNSS receivers captured the same signatures but showed up to 50 percent greater positioning degradation than geodetic-grade receivers, and multi-constellation precise point positioning reduced 3D errors by up to 23 percent for geodetic and 53 percent for low-cost receivers. Producer: four authors publishing in the MDPI journal Geosciences, issue 15(11), article 408, on 22 October 2025. Coverage: Mexican geodetic and low-cost stations during one storm. Access: gold open access; the abstract, authors and licence were taken from the OpenAlex record because the publisher page refused the cloud session. Licence and cost: CC BY per OpenAlex, free to read. Caveats: one storm and one country, and the station list and data files were not read here. Simulation uses: the error figures give exposure and resilience inputs for positioning-dependent infrastructure under extreme space weather. Related record: the Gannon storm GNSS degradation and agriculture loss case (case_study-gannon-storm-gnss-agriculture-losses-2024).
